text:
marta: Heads-up: planning to run the email_normalize_v2 schema + backfill during the change window tonight 23:00-01:00 UTC. Plan: add nullable column normalized_email, run batched backfill, then a short quiesce to apply not-null + index swap. Requesting a 60s quiesce window for the final swap. Ops doc: https://go/redwood/wiki/email-normalize

ali: Can you paste the exact migration id and which DB/shards will be targeted? Also we should pin the web service version for the swap window.

marta: db=users-db, migration_id=202603_email_normalize_v2. Backfill job: jobs/email_backfill:tag=2026-03. We'll stagger across 5 shards (user_0..user_4). Service pin: web -> tag/email-normalize-202603 for the swap minutes.

deploy-bot: migration canary scheduled: 2026-03-15T23:10Z on shard user_0. Canary steps: run backfill sample (10k rows), do small index validate, no quiesce. Will post status here.

sandeep: I'll run the canary and monitor "stallwatch" (lock wait) and CPU. Thresholds: lock_wait>120s or p95 write latency >300ms -> abort. I'll set autoscaled backfill rate cap to 500 qps for canary. @ops-oncall please watch replica lag.

ops-oncall: Oncall assigned for 23:00-01:00 UTC. I'll have replica_lag and disk_io alerts up: replica_lag>60s, io_util>85% -> page.

marta: Rollback checklist (short): 1) abort_backfill job, 2) unpin web services, 3) run fallback path (concurrent index create then swap view), 4) mark migration as failed and notify affected clients. Abort triggers: lock wait >120s, sustained p95 write >300ms, error rate spike >2x baseline. Documented in playbook.

ali: release-notes-bot can you add a short line "users: normalized_email column + backfill (migration 202603_email_normalize_v2)" to tonight's release notes?

release-notes-bot: note added -> https://go/redwood/releases/2026-03-15-notes#db

deploy-bot: canary passed on user_0. Observed max lock_wait=28s, p95 write latency delta +12ms. Proceeding to staged rollout: user_1 at 23:20Z, user_2 at 23:30Z with throttling. Backfill global cap=500 qps, per-shard cap=150 qps, batch_size=100.

sandeep: starting user_1 backfill now. I'll abort early if lock wait crosses 80s during any batch. Throttling in place.

ops-oncall: small CPU spike on user_2 at start, throttled backfill rate to 300 qps aggregate and it recovered. Replica lag stayed <20s.

marta: Reminder: we're using migration-lock-lease (2min TTL) during the final swap; it will soft-release on SIG. Swap will attempt to acquire lock, do quiesce, apply not-null and index rename, then release.

ali: Good to confirm swap mechanics. If swap fails, do we run rollback.sh and unpin right away? Need command in chat for oncall.

sandeep: Yes. Rollback command: `./ops/rollback_email_normalize.sh --migration 202603_email_normalize_v2 --unpin web` (this will stop backfill, unpin services, and revert any partial constraints). Keep an eye on the migration-lock-lease key.

deploy-bot: final swap scheduled for 23:55Z. Will broadcast events: swap_started, swap_done. Quiesce window: 60s.

deploy-bot: swap_started (automated)

deploy-bot: swap_done (automated)

marta: Verified post-swap checks: normalized_email populated, index present, no failed constraint messages in logs. Spot-checked a few user rows. Thanks all :rocket: 

ops-oncall: Confirmed replica lag normal and error rate steady. Monitoring for next 30m.

ali: I'll update the release note with next-day backward-compatibility note and service pin details.

marta: Closing thread — great coordination. Will follow up with runbook edits for the TTL and throttling knobs. :thumbsup:
